subject: gk
question: How many fundamental rights are provided by the Constitution as of November 2022?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**6**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Constitution** originally provided for **seven fundamental rights**.
 
• These were enumerated in **Part III** of the Constitution.
 
• However, the **44th Amendment Act** of **1978** abolished the **Right to Property** as a fundamental right.
 
• As of **November 2022**, there are **six fundamental rights** in the Indian Constitution.
 
• These rights are:
 
 
• **Right to Equality** (Articles 14-18)
 
• **Right to Freedom** (Articles 19-22)
 
• **Right against Exploitation** (Articles 23-24)
 
• **Right to Freedom of Religion** (Articles 25-28)
 
• **Cultural and Educational Rights** (Articles 29-30)
 
• **Right to Constitutional Remedies** (Article 32)
 
 
 
• The **Right to Property** was moved to **Article 300A** and made a **legal right**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Right to Property**__

 
 
• The **44th Amendment Act** of **1978** abolished the **Right to Property** as a fundamental right.
 
• It was then moved to **Article 300A** in **Part XII** of the Constitution.
 
• Now, it is a **legal right** rather than a fundamental right.
